items.title: The Clever Woman of the Family, by Charlotte M. Yonge
items.content: <article>An opinionated young woman seeks to prove her cleverness as she searches for a purpose in life.</article>

items.title: Cogewea, the Half-Blood, by Mourning Dove
items.content: <article>A young woman rancher of mixed Native American and European descent is wooed by the foreman and a newly-arrived tenderfoot.</article>

items.title: The House of Rimmon, by Henry van Dyke Jr.
items.content: <article>A Syrian general and a captive maid seek aid from the prophet Elisha.</article>

items.title: The Beggar’s Opera, by John Gay
items.content: <article>A highwayman worries that he’s undone when his love affairs are uncovered.</article>

items.title: The Great Airport Mystery, by Franklin W. Dixon
items.content: <article>After surviving an airplane accident, a pair of amateur sleuths get tangled up with a gang of thieves.</article>

items.title: The Home and the World, by Rabindranath Tagore
items.content: <article>When a wealthy Bengali woman’s husband invites an anti-British activist to their home, she becomes devoted to the nationalist cause, leading to disharmony in the household.</article>

items.title: Suspense, by Joseph Conrad
items.content: <article>A young Englishman stumbles upon love and political intrigue in Napoleonic-era Genoa.</article>

items.title: Hypatia, by Charles Kingsley
items.content: <article>A naive young monk in Roman Alexandria tries to convert a famous pagan woman philosopher to Christianity.</article>

items.title: ’Midst the Wild Carpathians, by Mór Jókai
items.content: <article>The newly-placed Prince of Transylvania must defend his realm against foreign influence.</article>

items.title: The Black Gang, by H. C. McNeile
items.content: <article>A soldier-turned-detective and his team bust up a Bolshevik plot to take over Britain.</article>

items.title: The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism, by Max Weber
items.content: <article>A German historian presents a theory detailing how certain ideas which are key to capitalism may have evolved from Protestantism.</article>

items.title: The Rescue, by Joseph Conrad
items.content: <article>The captain of a cargo ship is forced to rescue the passangers and crew of a yacht stranded on a Malaysian island.</article>

items.title: The Line of Love, by James Branch Cabell
items.content: <article>A generational saga plays out in a series of short stories about love and marriage in medieval Europe.</article>

items.title: The Fire in the Flint, by Walter White
items.content: <article>An optimistic Black physician returns to his Georgia hometown where he must grapple with racial tensions he thought had faded.</article>
